part.text:
The fix is complete and validated.

**Root cause:** In `fixedpoint_d2string()` (src/util.c:711), the leading-zero fill loop used the wrong bound (`i < fractional_digits` instead of `i < integer_digits + fractional_digits`). When the scaled value had fewer digits than `fractional_digits` (e.g. distance `0.0001` → scaled value `1` with 4 fractional digits), the second-to-last fractional byte was never written and the digit-writing loop only fills the last position — leaving uninitialized stack garbage in the reply, which is why `GEORADIUS ... WITHDIST` returned `b'0.00\xfc1'`.

**Fix:** corrected the fill-loop bound so all unwritten fractional positions are zero-filled, plus added regression assertions for `0.0001`/`0.00001` in the C unit test (`test_fixedpoint_d2string`).

**Validation:**
- `./runtest --single unit/geo` — all tests pass, including the failing `GEOSEARCH with small distance` test expecting `{1 0.0001} {2 9.8182}`
- Manual repro: 20 repeated `GEORADIUS ... WITHDIST` calls return `0.0001` every time
- `./runtest --single unit/type/zset` — passes (PASS_TO_PASS)
